Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Barcoded lineage tracing with sister-cell splitting
ideas.description: Tag cells with heritable lentiviral barcodes, split the population before drug exposure, and compare barcode enrichment among survivors across replicates. Like the material's list of rare words recurring at random, this tests whether persisters arise from pre-existing heritable states (the same barcodes recur) or from stochastic drug-induced switching (barcodes differ).

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome profiling before and after drug
ideas.description: Run paired scRNA-seq and ATAC-seq on untreated cells and on cells at several times after treatment. Identify rare pre-existing transcriptional or chromatin states, such as drug-efflux, stress-response or EMT-like programs, that predict survival, and confirm them by perturbing the key regulators.

ideas.title: Live-cell time-lapse imaging with reporters and retrospective omics
ideas.description: Image single cells for days with fluorescent reporters of signaling (ERK, p53), cell cycle and mitochondrial state, then follow which cells survive the drug. Fix and profile the survivors and their lineage relatives to link dynamic history, such as pulses or slow cycling, to survival.

ideas.title: Fluctuation-style kinetic analysis of state switching
ideas.description: Sort cells by a candidate marker, such as high or low expression, and measure how fast each subpopulation re-equilibrates and how its drug survival changes over time. Fit a Luria–Delbrück-type or Markov model to estimate switching rates, which distinguishes stable, slowly interconverting states from fast noise.

ideas.title: Metabolic and proteostasis phenotyping of persisters
ideas.description: Compare survivors and non-survivors for oxidative stress, mitochondrial activity, lipid peroxidation (ferroptosis sensitivity) and protein-homeostasis capacity. Use flow-based sensors, single-cell metabolomics and targeted inhibitors to test whether blocking the identified pathway selectively kills persisters.
